_note: Share splits and similar actions that change the number of shares without changing the value of a
holding. They matter for two reasons. First, the DSE serves prices exactly as they traded, so a split
shows up as a huge one-day fall that is not a loss: returns and therefore beta must be measured on a
split-adjusted series. Second, per-share figures from an annual report are on the share count of that
year, so comparing them with today's price needs the same basis.
Each action must carry the source it was verified from. No action is applied without one.

actions.detail: 1:10 share split. Listed ordinary shares rose from 500,000,000 to 5,000,000,000 and the nominal value per share fell from TZS 500,000 to TZS 50,000. Approved by the Capital Markets and Securities Authority on 2026-07-24. Trading was suspended 20 to 21 August 2026 while the register was updated, and post-split trading began on 2026-08-24.
evidence: DSE published prices for NMB: close TZS 17,700 on 2026-08-19, no trade on 2026-08-20 and 2026-08-21, close TZS 1,850 on 2026-08-24 (exactly one tenth), and shares in issue change from 500,000,000 to 5,000,000,000 on 2026-08-21.

known_source_errors.detail: The DSE's price rows report 5,000,000,000 shares on these two dates, before the split took effect on 2026-08-24, while the price on those days was still the pre-split level (TZS 14,990 and similar). These are errors in the source field. The field is not used for any calculation: the share count comes from the audited accounts and this file.
